newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki slips ahead of Nokia Q2, UPM very active.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki slips ahead of Nokia Q2, UPM very active.

text.p: Shares hovered down on Friday as Helsinki prepared for Nokia's Q2 report on Monday, the market closing before strong U.S. NAPM data sent U.S. markets sliding.
"If New York closes down one percent, that might point to profit-taking in Nokia before the results," one broker said after hours in Helsinki: the Dow Jones had shed 100 points.
The FOX portfolio index slipped 0.13 percent to 1,238.18, the all-share HEX fell 0.17 percent to 3,609.99. On the week, both showed a rise of one to two percent.
Big deals driven by overseas in forestry group UPM boosted overall volumes, but UPM was unchanged at 133.30 markka.
Nokia closed down 2.00 markka at 468.00 before its ADR came under slightly heavier pressure in New York after the NAPM data.
It has raced ahead since Swedish rival Ericsson last week delivered a major profit surprise, powered by handset growth, which in turn lifted expectations for Nokia.

A Reuters poll earlier this week showed expectations for Nokia's H1 pre-tax profit at a median 3.09 billion markka in a 2.97-3.30 billion range -- only a handful of analysts later publicly upgraded estimates further.
One broker saw a risk of profit-taking even on in-line figures -- but analysts note cellular is fundamentally powerful.

Metals and mining firm Outokumpu, normally a sedate performer, took a clear lift from investor perceptions of firm zinc prices and the strength of the dollar, brokers said: it rose 2.30 markka to 106.50 and made up seven percent of volume.
Outokumpu's gains helped limit the downside in the FOX index -- it contributed a positive 1.58 points, offsetting an overall 1.59 point fall, data from Reuters Securities 3000 showed.
The FOX's new composition -- Tamro, YIT and Asko replaced Finnair, TT Tieto and Cultor 2 -- gave a net negative 0.44 points, with Tamro and Asko off, and only YIT up.
